sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: PROGRESSIVE/SPLIT UPPER FLOW REGIME WILL PREVAIL OVER NORTH AMERICA TODAY. DEEP CONVECTIVE/SEVERE STORM POTENTIAL WILL BE TIED TO A MODERATELY MOIST WARM SECTOR AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT AND AMPLIFYING/POSITIVE TO NEUTRAL TILT UPPER TROUGH ADVANCING FROM THE UPPER MIDWEST/PLAINS TO THE MS RIVER VALLEY/ARKLATEX BY EARLY THURSDAY.

sections.title: GREAT LAKES/MIDWEST TO LA/COASTAL TX
sections.text: SHOWERS/TSTMS WILL BE ONGOING AT THE BEGINNING OF THE PERIOD ALONG/AHEAD OF AN EXTENSIVE NORTHEAST-SOUTHWEST ORIENTED COLD FRONT FROM THE MIDWEST/MIDDLE MS VALLEY TO THE ARKLATEX/TX HILL COUNTRY...WITH SOME ONGOING SEVERE POSSIBLE EARLY IN THE DAY. OTHERWISE...AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT AND EXISTING TSTMS/CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW...STRONG SOUTHWESTERLY MOISTURE TRANSPORT EARLY IN THE DAY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A MAINTENANCE/SOME NORTHEASTWARD EXPANSION OF MODERATE BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE INTO THE MIDWEST. THE NET RESULT IS EXPECTED TO BE PRE-COLD FRONTAL SURFACE DEWPOINTS BY AFTERNOON MAINLY IN THE UPPER 50S F ACROSS THE OHIO VALLEY...WITH LOWER 60S F COMMON ACROSS THE MID-SOUTH/ARKLATEX...WITH MID/SOME UPPER 60S F DEWPOINTS ALONG THE TX COAST. AMPLE LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT/SUSTAINED HEIGHT FALLS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AN UPSWING IN TSTM COVERAGE/RENEWED VIGOR DURING THE AFTERNOON WITHIN A MODERATELY UNSTABLE/WEAKLY CAPPED BOUNDARY LAYER AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT...WITH PRE-FRONTAL MLCAPE COMMONLY BETWEEN 750-1250 J/KG BY AFTERNOON. STRONG SPEED SHEAR...BUT LARGELY ORIENTED PARALLEL TO THE FRONT...IMPLIES ONLY A SHORT DURATION FOR SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLULAR DEVELOPMENT...WITH EMBEDDED-TYPE SU

sections.title: NORTHEAST STATES
sections.text: IN THE WAKE OF INITIAL SHORTWAVE RIDGING AND AN EASTWARD SHIFTING SURFACE LOW ACROSS NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND...ISOLATED TO PERHAPS SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD INCREASE ALONG THE SOUTHEASTWARD SAGGING COLD FRONT ACROSS /OR SPREAD INTO/ PORTIONS OF NORTHWEST PA AND NY/NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND. ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGE OF 55-65 KT WESTERLY MID LEVEL FLOW...STRONG BUT LARGELY UNIDIRECTIONAL SHEAR COULD SUPPORT SOME FAST MOVING SEMI-ORGANIZED LINE SEGMENTS CAPABLE OF HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS. HOWEVER...WITH THE POSSIBILITY OF RELATIVELY LIMITED DESTABILIZATION /500 J PER KG MLCAPE OR LESS/ AMIDST MID/UPPER 50S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS...A PARTICULARLY ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED SEVERE SCENARIO IS NOT CURRENTLY EXPECTED...SUCH THAT A CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK DOES NOT APPEAR WARRANTED. ..GUYER/GRAMS.. 04/07/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A SURFACE CYCLONE IN NE MO/W CENTRAL IL AS OF 11Z WILL MOVE ENEWD TO THE LOWER GREAT LAKES BY TONIGHT...AS A POSITIVE TILT MIDLEVEL TROUGH PROGRESSES EWD FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS TO THE MID MS VALLEY. TRAILING THE CYCLONE...A COLD FRONT WILL MOVE SEWD ACROSS IL/MO/AR/E TX BY LATE AFTERNOON...AND CONTINUE EWD/SEWD TO OH/KY/TN AND THE LOWER MS VALLEY BY EARLY THURSDAY. THIS COLD FRONT WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY FOCUS FOR STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE PERIOD.

sections.title: OH/MS VALLEY REGION THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: CONVECTION INVOF THE COLD FRONT HAS LARGELY DISSIPATED...LEAVING SCATTERED DEBRIS CLOUDS FROM AR NEWD TO THE OH VALLEY. BREAKS IN THE CLOUDS WILL ALLOW DAYTIME HEATING AND ASSOCIATED LOW-LEVEL DESTABILIZATION. ALSO...LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE DEPTH/QUALITY HAS IMPROVED SINCE YESTERDAY ACROSS E TX/LA/AR WHERE BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS RANGE FROM THE LOW-MID 60S. THIS MOISTURE WILL SPREAD NEWD IN ADVANCE OF THE COLD FRONT TODAY...WITH DEWPOINTS EXPECTED TO INCREASE INTO THE LOW 60S BY AFTERNOON AS FAR NE AS IL/INDIANA. STILL...THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY WILL BE TEMPERED SOMEWHAT BY WEAKER MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES COMPARED TO PREVIOUS DAYS. THE NET RESULT SHOULD BE PRE-FRONTAL CORRIDOR OF 750-1250 MLCAPE BY MID AFTERNOON. THUNDERSTORMS WILL INCREASE IN COVERAGE/INTENSITY RATHER QUICKLY BY EARLY-MID AFTERNOON AS LINGERING CONVECTIVE INHIBITION IS REMOVED IN THE BELT OF ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT. WIND PROFILES ARE EXPECTED TO BECOME MORE UNIDIRECTIONAL WITH TIME...AND LOW-LEVEL FLOW/SHEAR WILL ALSO BECOME RATHER MODEST IN THE WARM SECTOR BY AFTERNOON. THE LARGELY FRONT-PARALLEL SHEAR VECTORS AND FLOW ALOFT WILL PROMOTE RATHER QUICK EVOLUTION INTO LINE SEGMENTS...THOUGH DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR/INSTABI

sections.title: IL/IND
sections.text: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS BREAKS IN THE CLOUDS ACROSS CENTRAL IL IN VICINITY OF THE WARM FRONT. LOW LEVEL MOISTURE IS ALSO INCREASING FROM THE SOUTH...WHICH SHOULD LEAD TO AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 500-1000 J/KG IN THE REGION. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM AHEAD OF THE SURFACE LOW...BOTH ALONG THE WARM FRONT AND IN THE WARM SECTOR. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW STRONG EFFECTIVE SHEAR AND SUFFICIENT CAPE FOR SUPERCELL STORMS. MESOSCALE MODELS ALSO INDICATE THIS REGION IS MOST LIKELY TO SEE DISCRETE INITIATION. LOW LEVEL VERTICAL SHEAR IS MODEST BUT SUFFICIENT FOR A RISK OF ISOLATED TORNADOES...ALONG WITH HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS AS STORMS TRACK EASTWARD INTO IND.

sections.title: AR/MS/TN INTO OH VALLEY
sections.text: SURFACE COLD FRONT OVER AR/LA/TX WILL LIKELY PROVIDE THE LOW LEVEL LIFT FOR A LINE OF SEVERE STORMS LATER TODAY. THIS ACTIVITY WILL SPREAD NORTHEASTWARD INTO PARTS OF MS/TN/KY THROUGH THE EVENING HOURS. A WEAK CAP COULD CONTRIBUTE TO A RISK OF DISCRETE SUPERCELLS EARLY IN THE EVENT...BUT LINEAR STRUCTURES WITH EMBEDDED BOW/LEWPS ARE EXPECTED THIS EVENING. DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL APPEAR TO BE THE MAIN THREATS...ALTHOUGH ISOLATED TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT. ..HART/HURLBUT.. 04/07/2010

sections.title: LOWER-MID MS VALLEY TO LOWER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: BACK EDGE OF GEN TSTM AND SVR OUTLOOK LINES HAVE BEEN ADJUSTED SLIGHTLY BASED ON LATEST CONVECTIVE TRENDS...WITH ACTIVITY EXPECTED TO SHIFT GENERALLY EWD ACROSS OUTLOOK AREAS THROUGH REMAINDER PERIOD AS DESCRIBED BEFORE. BKN LINES OF STG-SVR TSTMS...GROWING IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY FROM IL SWWD TO ARKLATEX REGION AS THEY MOVE INTO DESTABILIZING AIR MASS...ARE COVERED WITHIN SPC WWS 61/62. REF THOSE PRODUCTS AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR NEAR-TERM SVR UPDATES WITH THIS ACTIVITY. ..EDWARDS.. 04/07/2010 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1108 AM CDT WED APR 07 2010/ 16Z SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS A LOW ALONG THE MO/IL BORDER AND A WARM FRONT EXTENDING NORTHEASTWARD INTO IL/IND AND NORTHWEST OH. A COLD FRONT EXTENDS SOUTHWARD FROM THE LOW INTO NORTHWEST AR/SOUTHEAST OK AND EASTERN TX. BOTH OF THESE BOUNDARIES WILL TEND TO FOCUS STRONG/SEVERE STORMS LATER TODAY.
